analysis: Only docs/architecture/inference.md changed, and the supplied units are BASE text for lines 1236-1777; no executable code changed. I examined the visible base text of the MiMo V2.6 native candidate, Flash-Next ownership, coordinator-serving channels, invariants and code-map sections, plus the changed-range map and the single patch excerpt, which is truncated. The one visible hunk (head line 607) adds a documentation phrase that a refused SSD store's typed reason reaches the bridge for local /metrics only. That relates to T-041 (prefix-cache SSD tier), but the supplied evidence shows no code change and no new exposure. The documentation states the reason is local-only and content-free, so a possible leak of cache-store state is not established. Head-side ranges (617-856, 1457-1465, 1494-1514, 1797-1822, 2071-2078) were not supplied as text, so the remainder of the head content is unverified. The base text I reviewed describes controls consistent with the threat model: coordinator-hop-by-hop encryption of provider output, content-free client errors, media decode bounds, and no payload disk writes for in-memory video. I found no documented weakening of the T-041 mitigations (HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, account-scoped salt). Remaining integration question: whether the truncated and unsupplied head hunks, especially the 617-856 insertion, introduce security-relevant claims that contradict the threat model, e.g. on /metrics exposure, cache TTL or salt scoping, and whether the code behind the /metrics statement matches it. Treat this as a low-risk documentation-only change with incomplete head coverage.
